charter.question: Capability owned
charter.answer: Agent definitions and execution, run persistence, model-provider and outbound MCP integration, and the opt-in local operator principal plus Bimaaji agent tool adapters. The #2653 supplement reviews only the local operator and adapter boundary.
charter.evidence: packages/ai-agent/composer.json; package provider manifest; src/LocalOperator; Tool/Bimaaji

charter.question: Excluded capability
charter.answer: CLI stdio framing, client configuration, project initialization and the transport-neutral shared tool catalogue belong to cli, bimaaji/ai-development, site-contract and ai-tools.

charter.question: Consumers and composition
charter.answer: Kernel provider discovery composes the optional agent runtime in development installations; CLI stdio uses LocalOperatorPrincipal. Generated applications and split users need independent qualification. The no-dev root closure removes ai-agent.
charter.evidence: composer.json extra.waaseyaa.providers; cli McpServeCommand; #2658; candidate-local tests

charter.question: Dependencies and adapters
charter.answer: Requires ai-tools, bimaaji, access, foundation, audit, persistence and HTTP clients, among others; wayfinding is suggested. Agent adapters delegate to Bimaaji services. HTTP MCP delegation is outbound and outside this supplement.

charter.question: Public surface and lifecycle
charter.answer: The editable declaration names 18 public and one internal symbol. Many other exports are @api-only or unclassified; their caller and lifecycle obligations are not settled. LocalOperatorPrincipal requires explicit CLI development transport attestation and refuses serialization or ambient account context.

charter.question: Supported profiles and observable evidence
charter.answer: Source-local local-operator tests pass and no-dev removes the optional package in a published consumer. Exact-base generated application, standalone split and packaged coding-client qualification are pending. Do not infer installed success from source tests.

findings.title: Default null model provider can complete an agent run without a model response
findings.observed: MessagingServiceProvider binds NullLlmProvider by default; the provider returns a normal end_turn placeholder and current integration expectations allow Completed. The existing #1608 issue tracks this behavior.
findings.expected_contract: A run that has no configured usable model should expose an explicit unavailable/refusal outcome rather than a normal model completion.
findings.consequence: A caller of the optional agent runtime can treat a no-model run as completed work. Local stdio graph inspection does not invoke a model and is unaffected.
findings.refutation: No complete independent rederivation/refutation pair ran for this bounded pass. The placeholder could be intentional for a documented demo profile, but the normal Completed result still needs contract review.
findings.disposition: repair after independent verification under existing #1608
findings.dependencies: Confirm supported no-model and demo contracts before runtime change.
findings.acceptance: With no configured model, an installed agent run produces a distinct non-success outcome and no success-shaped content; configured model behavior and local stdio inspection remain intact.
findings.residual_risk: No-model production exposure and split-consumer behavior have not been qualified.
findings.next_action: The ai-agent audit owner obtains independent tier-A rederivation and refutation under #1608.
findings.consumer_unblock: independent: this does not block local stdio inspection under #2653

verification.performed: Source and existing test expectations observed by one boundary investigator; tier-A pair pending.

findings.notes: Existing issue, not a new #2653 blocker.

findings.title: Agent package README describes an obsolete four-tool Bimaaji catalogue
findings.observed: The ai-agent README lists four Bimaaji tool adapters, while source and the local profile include SearchSpecsTool as the fifth adapter. It also does not identify the absent default corpus for search.
findings.expected_contract: Consumer guidance should distinguish five registered adapters, three default local inspection tools, and the corpus prerequisite for useful search.
findings.consequence: A developer can infer that search is not supplied or that discoverable search has a usable packaged corpus.
findings.refutation: The README table may describe the older embedded demo rather than the default local profile, but it says four adapters and source now contains five. The two profile counts must be stated separately.
findings.disposition: document in a bounded #3118 package documentation slice
findings.dependencies: Confirm #2661 corpus packaging acceptance before describing search as usable by default.
findings.acceptance: README names five source adapters, identifies the three local defaults and the absent/default corpus accurately, and linked live specs use current ai-tools registry ownership.
findings.residual_risk: The full package public-surface and live spec review remain pending.
findings.next_action: The ai-agent audit owner requests one independent tier-B verification and reconciles this with the existing #3118 documentation owner.
findings.consumer_unblock: independent: documentation correction is separate from first stdio descriptor slice

verification.performed: One boundary investigator compared README with package source; independent tier-B review pending.
